full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Quddus, J: This Rule Nisi, at the instance of a legal heir of a judgment debtor in a mortgage decree, was issued calling in question orders dated 1.7.2009 and 6.9.2009 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, Faridpur in Artha Rin Execution Case No.104 of 2005 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit No.10 of 2004) issuing certificate of title in favour of the decree holder-bank under section 33(7) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (herein after referred to ‘the Ain’) in respect of the mortgaged property. 

 Facts leading to this writ petition, in short, are that Islami Bank Bangladesh Ltd., Khulna Branch as plaintiff instituted Artha Rin Suit No.10 of 2004 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Faridpur for recovery of loan amounting to Taka 4,01,55,468.00 (four crore one lac fifty-five thousand four hundred sixty-eight) only. The defaulting-borrower, Md. Aminuzzaman, Proprietor of M/S M. A. Zaman and his mother Mrs. Khodeja Zaman being third party mortgager were made defendant Nos.1 and 2 respectively in the suit. Although defendant No.1 (Md. Aminuzzaman) entered into appearance, did not contest the suit and as a result it was decreed exparte on 8.5.2005. Thereafter the decree holder-bank filed Artha Rin Execution Case No.104 of 2005 in the Artha Rin Adalat, Faridpur on 19.6.2005. In course of proceedings in the said execution case, auction notices were published under section 33 (1) (4) of the Ain and attempts were made twice to sell the mortgaged property. As no bidder participated in the said auctions, the decree holder-bank filed an application on 22.7.2008 for issuance of a certificate of title in its favour under section 33 (7) of the Ain. When the said application was pending, both the parties tried to resolve the dispute through mutual compromise, but failed. Ultimately the learned Judge of the executing Court allowed the said application by order dated 1.7.2009. The judgment debtor filed an application on 5.7.2009 for time to pay all outstanding dues and in the meantime to postpone issuance of the certificate. The learned Judge allowed him time to pay the outstanding dues by order dated 30.7.2009 and fixed 6.9.2009 for deposition of the money and hearing of the said application. As the judgment debtor failed to deposit the money even to take any step on the next date, the learned Judge by his order dated 6.9.2009 rejected the application dated 5.7.2009 and passed an order to prepare the certificate. Subsequently the learned Judge issued/signed the certificate on 9.9.2009 and sent it for registration on 29.9.2009 (vide annexe:D-1, order sheet of the execution case). Thereafter the execution proceeding was in progress for delivery of possession, when the present petitioner as a heir of Khodeja Zaman (defendant No.2-judgment debtor) filed an application on 5.9.2010 for staying operation of the certificate and allow him to pay ¼ of the outstanding dues within one month and to pay the remaining dues by eight installment (vide annexe-D to the writ petition). In the said application the writ petitioner stated inter alia, that he is the younger brother of defendant No.1 and son of defendant No.2; that his mother, defendant No.2 did not execute any mortgage deed in favour of the respondent-bank; that he was in dark about the execution proceedings; that the petitioner, his three brothers and five sisters inherited the mortgaged property of their mother Khodeja Zaman (defendant No.2), since deceased; that his parents’ grave yards were situated on the mortgaged land; that Title Suit No.24 of 2010 for partition of the land allegedly mortgaged by defendant No.2 was pending before the First Court of Joint District Judge, Faridpur and the respondent-bank was made a defendant therein. 

 The learned Judge of the executing Court deferred hearing of the said application dated 5.9.2010 to the next date on 16.9.2010. On the next date the decree-holder bank filed an application for disposal of the execution case under section 33 (9) of the Ain and the judgment debtor filed money receipt showing payment of Taka 1,25,00,000/= (one crore twenty-five lac) only in favour of the decree holder-bank. Meanwhile the bank had sold 8.57 acres of mortgaged land to respondent Nos.3-5 by three separate registered sale deeds, under which circumstances, the writ petitioner moved the present writ petition before this Court challenging orders dated 1.7.2009 and 6.9.2009 passed in the execution case, obtained a Rule and an order of stay on 10.10.2010 subject to payment of Taka 2,00,00,000/= (two crore) only on or before 30th December, 2010. Subsequently he had deposited the said amount in favour of the respondent-bank and filed an affidavit to that effect. 

 Respondent Nos.3-5, subsequent purchasers from the decree holder-bank, have appeared and contested the Rule by filling an affidavit-in-opposition contending inter alia that the petitioner did not take any proper step in time, missed all opportunities given by the executing Court and has come to this Court at a belated stage after completion of transfer of the mortgaged property in favour of the decree holder-bank by issuance of the certificate on 9.9.2009 and registration of the same on 29.9.2009; that he has come to this Court after one year from registration and transfer of the mortgaged property only to drag the matter and deprive these respondents from enjoyment of their lawful property, which they purchased from the bank for valuable consideration; that the plaint in Title Suit No.24 of 2010 for partition had already been rejected by order dated 5.9.2010 passed by the Joint District Judge, First Court, Faridpur on an application filed by the respondent-bank. 

 Mr. Abdul Baset Majumder, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that in the present case the decree holder-bank without selling first the borrower’s property attracted the property of the third party mortgagor violating the provision of section 6(5) of the Ain and that the executing Court issued certificate without assessing the accurate price of the mortgaged property under section 12 (6) (7) of the Ain and as such the impugned order issuing certificate of title under section 33 (7) of the Ain in favour of the decree holder-bank is illegal and without lawful authority. The petitioner is having his parents’ grave yards on the mortgaged land and since the execution case is still pending and registration of the certificate has not yet been completed, there is scope to release the property on payment of the remaining outstanding dues to meet the ends of justice. He further submits that the present petitioner is neither a borrower, nor a mortgager or guarantor, but inherited the property of defendant No.2-judgment debtor and as such he has every right to redeem the property allegedly mortgaged by his mother. Lastly he submits that the mortgaged property has been sold to respondent Nos.3-5 at shokingly low price and it has been done malafide in collusion with the corrupt bank officials, and this Court should interfere into the impugned orders to ensure just and faire play. 

 Mrs. Fowzia Karim Firoze, the learned Advocate appearing for respondent Nos.3-5, opposes the Rule and submits that the certificate has been issued in favour of the decree holder-bank in due process of law and there is nothing arbitrarily or malafide or anything done in violation of law. The petitioner being a heir of the judgment-debtor had full knowledge of the suit as well as of the execution case. He has lost his right to redeem the property mortgaged by his predecessor-in-interest, with issuance of certificate of title in favour of the bank. 

 We have examined the writ petition, affidavit-in-opposition and other materials on record. It appears from the order sheet of the execution case, that notice under section 30 of the Ain was duly served; that defendant No.1-judgment debtor was given ample opportunity to pay off the loan and release the property, but without doing so he dragged the matter for years together by moving various applications on this and that plea. He had moved writ petition before the High Court Division and kept the execution case stayed for two years, but ultimately allowed it to be discharged for default. In the execution proceeding auction notices were published in four news papers, and attempts were made twice to sell the mortgaged property. As no bidder had participated in the bid, the decree-holder bank filed application for issuance of certificate in its favour under section 33(7) of the Ain, and the executing Court allowed the same by the impugned order. It is reasonably presumed that summons of the suit was served upon defendant No.2, who did not appear. Defendant No.1 though had appeared, did not contest the suit and allowed it to be decreed exparte. The petitioner is mysteriously silent as to when defendant No.2-judgment debtor died, before or after issuance of the certificate. It also does not appear from the order sheet of the execution case that after death of defendant No.2, the present petitioner was made a party in the execution case either at the instance of the decree holder-bank or on his own motion. 

 We have also examined the application dated 5.9.2010 filed by the petitioner (vide annexe-D to the writ petition) and also the plaint in Title Suit No. 24 of 2010, which he instituted for partition of the mortgaged property (vide annexe-4 series to the affidavit-in-opposition). The statement about his first knowledge of the mortgage decree, or of the execution case is not clear and specified. In the plaint he admitted the mortgage deed to have been executed by his mother and stated that he came to learn about the mortgage decree for the first time in April, 2010. But in the application dated 5.9.2010 he denied execution of any mortgage deed by his mother and did not clearly mention anything as to how he learnt about the decree. It is difficult to believe that the petitioner had no knowledge of the execution case, or of the mortgage decree under the facts and circumstances of the present case, specially when the defendants are his brother and mother respectively. 

 It is also pertinent that the petitioner has challenged orders dated 1.7.2009 and 6.9.2009 in the present writ petition. But he is not a party in the Artha Rin Suit or in the Execution Case. The executing Court passed the impugned order dated 1.7.2009 on an application filed by the decree holder bank, while by order dated 6.9.2009 the Court rejected an application of defendant No.1-judgment debtor. The present petitioner appeared in the scenario for the first time on 5.9.2010 and without being a party in the execution case filed application for staying operation of the certificate. 

 It appears that after issuance of the certificate under section 33 (7) of the Ain, it was presented for registration on 29.9.2009 and subsequently the mortgaged property was sold to respondent Nos.3-5. The mortgage decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat attained in finality with issuance of the certificate. It is a settled principle of law that after attainment of a mortgage decree in finality, the mortgagor-judgment debtor loses his right to redeem the mortgaged property. The law invests authority in Court to issue certificate of title in an execution proceeding under the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, if the mortgaged property cannot be sold in auction. There is nothing wrong in issuance of certificate under section 33(7) of the Ain under the facts and circumstances of the present case. Defendant No.1-judgment debtor filed application dated 5.7.2009 for release of the auctioned property without depositing the decretal money, still the executing Court gave him opportunity to pay off the money and postponed issuance of certificate for time being. But he failed to pay the decretal money within the time given by the Court, even did not take any step whatsoever on the next date, as a result the executing Court by order dated 6.9.2009 rejected the application dated 5.7.2009, which appears to have been rightly done. 

 The executing Court/respondent-bank is directed to return the money to the petitioner or the judgment debtor as the case may be, which have been deposited by them in favour of the decree holder-bank after issuance of the certificate.
